Name: Indogulf BioAg
Description:
Indogulf BioAg is a biotechnology company focused on one thing — bringing biology back into industrial systems at scale.

While our primary work lies in agriculture, we also operate in niche biological applications across the mining and environmental sectors, where microbial solutions can drive more sustainable and efficient processes.

We work with microbial species not just as inputs, but as tools to solve real-world problems — improving nutrient efficiency, restoring soil health, enabling bioleaching, and supporting bioremediation.

Our foundation is technical. We operate across research, product development, regulatory, industrial-scale manufacturing, and global distribution — enabling us to move from lab to field with speed, control, and consistency.

The technology platform includes microbial fermentation, botanical extraction, and nano-encapsulation — enabling the design and delivery of high-performance biological formulations across applications.

We partner with ag companies, distributors, and industrial players to develop and commercialise biological solutions — from single-species actives to complex consortia. The work spans biofertilisers, biostimulants, biocontrol, and emerging industrial use cases, supported by strong QC systems, regulatory understanding, and field validation.

We are building Indogulf BioAg to be a long-term player — grounded in science, driven by execution, and committed to delivering solutions that perform.

If you’re passionate about bringing better biological solutions to market — we’d like to hear from you.

Name: altona Diagnostics #BeNeLux
Description:
WIE ZIJN WIJ / QUI SOMMES-NOUS ?
altona Diagnostics is een medisch diagnostisch bedrijf dat in vitro diagnostische testen ontwikkelt en produceert voor de PCR-gebaseerde detectie van pathogenen zoals virussen, bacteriën of parasieten. altona Diagnostics, met hoofdkantoor in Hamburg-Altona, Duitsland, is particulier eigendom en heeft wereldwijd meer dan 350 mensen in dienst. Het bedrijf is al meer dan 20 jaar actief in de moleculaire diagnostiek en is ISO 13485-gecertificeerd. altona Diagnostics verkoopt zijn geregistreerde producten aan particuliere en klinische laboratoria wereldwijd via dochterondernemingen en meer dan 40 distributiepartners.

altona Diagnostics est une entreprise spécialisée dans le diagnostic médical qui conçoit et fabrique des tests de diagnostiques in-vitro pour la détection par PCR des agents pathogènes tels que les virus, les bactéries et les parasites. Basée dans le district d’Altona à Hambourg en Allemagne, altona Diagnostics appartient à des propriétaires privés et emploie plus de 350 personnes dans le monde. L’entreprise fait partie du secteur du diagnostic moléculaire depuis plus de 20 ans et détient une certification ISO 13485. altona Diagnostics vend ses produits enregistrés à des laboratoires privés et cliniques à l’international par l’intermédiaire de filiales et plus de 40 partenaires de distribution.

Name: MucosaTec
Description: MucosaTec is a German biotech start-up developing next-generation, locally acting therapeutics for infectious diseases. Our vision is to strengthen the natural barrier function of mucus and enable rapid, immune-independent protection at mucosal surfaces, with a special focus on influenza. Our versatile platform technology enables us to actively broaden our pipeline to additional pathogens, addressing unmet medical needs across infectious diseases.

Name: Healthy Crops
Description:
The Healthy Crops Project is an international research project with the aim to achieve significant yield increases for small scale producers in Africa and Asia by providing disease resistant rice varieties that can be introgressed with local elite lines.

To reach our goals we already developed a strategy to combat bacterial blight (BB) of rice, one of the most devastating rice diseases with a significant impact on small scale producers in low and middle-income countries. The team has already successfully generated BB-resistant rice lines and created a diagnostic toolbox that enables a rapid disease diagnosis of the newly occurring pathogenic bacterial strains (both published in Nature Biotechnology in 2019). Recently, the team further reported the discovery of a blight outbreak in Tanzania and presented a modified an African rice variety resistant to the pathogen.

By now, we are working on a broad range of disease resistance that we want to offer to smallholder farmers in future.

Name: Terrificproject
Description: Supported by CBEJ U, the TERRIFIC project aims to reshape the European Circular Bioeconomy through eight innovative bio-based solutions that will transform the food packaging sector. Bringing together 19 top partners from 9 EU countries, with leadership from Novamont, this forward-thinking initiative is set to drive progress in sustainable and functional packaging. Over the next four years, a state-of-the-art biorefinery will be established—the first of its kind—serving as a center for developing versatile bio-based materials. These materials will underpin advanced packaging solutions designed not only to protect and extend food shelf life but also to enhance transportability and support multiple end-of-life options, from composting to recycling, thus offering opportunities for economic growth while ensuring social and environmental sustainability.

Name: LifeGlimmer GmbH
Description:
LifeGlimmer designs decision support systems, digital twins, and data-driven engineering workflows for biotechnology and biomanufacturing.

We help research groups, industrial partners, and EU consortia turn complex biological and process data into operational decisions: what to design, what to test, how to scale, and where to reduce risk.

Our work connects systems biology, bioinformatics, machine learning, process modelling, and software engineering. We build the data and decision layer needed to move from trial-and-error experimentation toward predictive, automated, and sustainable bioproduction.

Core areas include decision support systems, digital twins, ML and AI frameworks, multi-omics integration, genome-scale metabolic modelling, DBTL automation, FAIR data workflows, data fabric, knowledge graphs, bioprospecting, LCA, TEA, Safe and Sustainable by Design, and EU project coordination.

LifeGlimmer works at the interface between the wet lab and the data centre, building models, dashboards, pipelines, and decision workflows that scientific and industrial teams can actually use.

Description:
ARTCLINE GmbH develops innovative therapy methods for intensive care medicine based on immune cells. Our current main project is the development of the so-called ARTICE technology for the treatment of bacterial sepsis.

ARTCLINE's vision is the development of innovative immune cell-based therapy approaches and to make the technology available to physicians and hospitals worldwide. The safety and effectiveness of the therapy is our top priority.

Our extensive cell biological, clinical and industrial experience in the fields of immunology, sepsis diagnostics and therapy help us to realize our vision. Together with scientists and partners, we focus our research activities on the root causes and correlations of sepsis.

For many years, the founders and the team of ARTCLINE GmbH have been successfully involved in the transfer of medical inventions from university research to industrial application. We have an extensive network and long standing experience in the development and successful marketing of medical devices and drugs.

Description:
DECENTRALIZING BIOGAS. REDEFINING WASTE.

Food waste disposal today is expensive, unhygienic, and energy-intensive. Our Smart-Degrader replaces costly and carbon-heavy disposal processes with a plug-and-play solution that generates energy and liquid fertilizer right where waste is produced – on-site, clean, and odor-free.

With seamless integration into existing heating systems, our system empowers hotels, restaurants, canteens, small farms, and educational institutions to cut waste costs, lower emissions, and move toward a circularity & energy autonomy.

 Save up to 15.000 € every year on disposal

Name: BioeXsen GmbH
Description:
Abläufe in der Molekulardiagnostik sind häufig zeitaufwendig, personalintensiv und mit biologischen Risiken verbunden.

Ob Labor, Klinik oder Praxis - BioeXsen liefert zuverlässige Tools für eine moderne, flexible Diagnostik.

Name: OakLabs Scientific
Description: At OakLabs Scientific, we believe that each of us can live longer healthy. In a society where individual healthcare is increasingly challenging, we are pioneering ways to detect and avert disease before it occurs. Using our unique Artificial Intelligence algorithms and high-molecular-weight data, we are exploring individual health status in unprecedented depth.

Name: Modulux3D
Description:
At Modulux3D, we are redefining how new medicines and consumer products are tested before reaching patients and consumers.

Born from cutting-edge research at Goethe University Frankfurt and the EU Horizon projects BRIGHTER and B-BRIGHTER, Modulux3D develops next-generation 3D bioprinting and AI-driven tissue model platforms that replicate human biology with unprecedented precision and longevity.

Our flagship technology, the LUMINATE 3D bioprinter, fabricates complex, high-resolution tissue constructs (e.g., skin, liver, gut) using advanced light-sheet printing and adaptive AI quality control. Combined with our proprietary OptiPrintAI software (Distr@l funded), we enable fully automated quality control and reproducible tissue production, setting new standards for predictive, regulatory-ready in vitro testing.

 Why we’re different:

Long-lived, physiologically accurate models that mimic real human tissues for weeks (supporting chronic exposure and recovery studies).

AI-based quality control ensures every construct meets strict reproducibility and compliance criteria, addressing one of the biggest limitations in current 3D culture technologies.

Modular hardware ecosystem: printers, organ models, and analytics — that integrates seamlessly into pharma and consumer-care R&D workflows.

Regulatory alignment with OECD and ISO test guidelines bridging the gap between research and regulatory acceptance.

By combining biophotonics, tissue engineering, and artificial intelligence, we empower pharmaceutical and consumer goods companies to replace unreliable animal testing with human-relevant, high-throughput models, ultimately bringing safer, more effective therapies to patients faster.

Name: Department of Bioprocess Engineering - University of Hohenheim
Description:
Welcome to the Official Page of the Department of Bioprocess Engineering, University of Hohenheim! 

Discover the cutting-edge world of Bioprocess Engineering at the Institute of Food Science and Biotechnology. Our department is dedicated to advancing knowledge and innovation in biomanufacturing and bioeconomy, where science meets sustainable solutions. 

The Department of Bioprocess Engineering at the University of Hohenheim is under the leadership of Prof. Dr. Hausmann, a distinguished expert in the field. Committed to excellence in research and application of integrated bioprocess engineering, our department comprises experts who lead projects at the forefront of bioprocessing. 

State-of-the-Art Laboratories:
Explore our well-equipped laboratories, including a state-of-the-art Molecular Biology Lab. Here, students and researchers delve into the intricacies of genetic engineering of bacteria, advancing our understanding of biotechnology at the molecular level. 
Bioreactors: Immerse yourself in our bioprocessing capabilities with a line of 3 advanced 42-liter bioreactors. These cutting-edge systems provide a platform for scalable and efficient production processes, ensuring students receive hands-on experience with industrial-scale technology. 
Analytical Instruments: Benefit from our analytical prowess with instruments like HPTLC, HPLC, MPLS, and more. These tools empower our researchers to analyze and optimize bioprocesses, ensuring precision in every stage of development.

Interdisciplinary Approach: We believe in the power of collaboration. Our department fosters interdisciplinary research!

Name: AF-B-STEP
Description:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common heart rhythm disorder that becomes more prevalent with age, affecting about one in three people by age 55. It can lead to serious health problems, including stroke, heart failure, and premature death. Overall, AF accounts for up to 2–3% of all healthcare costs in Europe and North America (1, 2). Currently, AF is mostly diagnosed as simple “yes” or “no”, which lacks precision and often leads to confusion or anxiety in patients, especially when minor episodes are detected by pacemakers or by wearables, such as smartwatches.

AF-B-STEP is an international research project that brings together hospitals, universities, industry partners, patient groups, and healthcare payors to improve how AF is measured, quantified, and treated. The consortium will analyse data from more than 100,000 people to estimate the population-wide burden of AF, identify which types of AF pose the greatest risk, and determine how AF burden increases likelihood of stroke or heart failure. It will also establish standards for how medical devices and consumer wearables should measure and report AF.

The findings will help clinicians make informed decisions on diagnosis and treatment, support better healthcare decisions, and guide European innovation and regulation. Ultimately, AF-B-STEP aims to reduce AF-related deaths and disability, improve the patients’ quality of life, and lower healthcare costs.

Name: PicoScreen
Description:
The demand for highly efficient enzymes is rapidly increasing across multiple industries — from biotechnology and chemicals to food, materials, and sustainability-driven applications. However, enzyme discovery and optimization are increasingly constrained by the limits of existing screening technologies.

Today’s standard screening approaches are often slow, labor-intensive, and costly, requiring significant manual effort and limiting the number of variants that can be evaluated. While ultra-high-throughput methods exist in research settings, they are rarely adopted in industry, as increased throughput often comes at the expense of data quality, robustness, and reproducibility.

We have developed an ultra-high-throughput enzyme screening technology designed specifically to overcome these limitations. Our approach enables a step-change in screening efficiency while delivering scientifically robust, reproducible results. This allows enzyme companies to scale their screening capacity without compromising quality — making our technology compatible with real-world industrial screening workflows, with quality at the core.

Our founding team has deep expertise in enzyme screening with two team members being post-doctoral researchers in biotechnology, ensuring scientific excellence and reproducibility. Complementing this, our third team member brings business expertise from an early-stage biotech startup, with a background in innovative business development and research on risk-based decision-making — helping customers make confident, data-driven choices.

We are currently engaging with enzyme companies, R&D teams, and partners interested in scaling enzyme discovery and optimization — and with investors who share our vision of enabling the next generation of industrial biocatalysis. Let’s talk!

Name: Imaginary Biolabs
Description:
Biology is becoming programmable, but the way we design biological systems has not yet caught up. Most development still relies on fragmented tools, inconsistent data, and experimental trial-and-error. 

Imaginary Biolabs is building the AI infrastructure to change this. We develop a unified computational platform for designing biomolecules, where data, models, and evaluation form a coherent system rather than a collection of disconnected components.

At its core is a simple shift: from experimentation-first to computation-first development. Instead of testing ideas primarily in the lab, biological systems can be designed, iterated, and refined in silico before entering experimental validation. This makes development faster, more systematic, and significantly more resource-efficient.

Enabling this requires a foundation that biological machine learning has been missing: structured data pipelines, reproducible benchmarks, and integrated access to models. When these elements are brought together, it becomes possible to build, benchmark, and deploy machine learning models for biomolecular design in a consistent and scalable way.

This creates an environment where models can be applied directly to real design problems, new approaches can be developed and evaluated on shared foundations, and a larger part of biological development can move into computation — shortening cycles, improving success rates, and opening up new classes of biological solutions.

Over time, this infrastructure becomes more than a tool. It becomes the software layer between an idea and its biological product — a virtual laboratory where biological systems can be engineered with the same level of control and iteration as software systems.

Our first milestone is establishing reliable foundations for biomolecular machine learning, enabling models to be built, compared, and improved on consistent grounds. Long-term, we aim to design increasingly complex biological systems at scale.

Description:
Quantum Leap is an academic initiative under the UnternehmerTUM - Academy for Innovators in the scope of the Tech Challenge course. Our mission is to create new products in the field of medicine using the so-called quantum diamonds sensors technologies.

Quantum diamond sensing uses the exceptional properties of diamonds at the quantum level to enhance medical diagnostics and sensing capabilities. By embedding tiny diamond sensors into medical devices, these sensors can detect and measure extremely small changes in temperature, magnetic fields, and electric fields. This heightened sensitivity allows for more accurate monitoring of biological processes, such as detecting early-stage diseases, tracking drug interactions, monitoring patient vital signs, etc.

At Quantum Leap, we believe quantum diamond sensing technology has the potential to revolutionize medical research and clinical practice by providing precise and real-time information, leading to improved diagnostics, personalized treatments, and better patient outcomes.

Name: AIPD Lab
Description:
Our lab focuses on AI-Guided Protein Design to engineer cellular decision-making, with the goal of creating synthetic proteins that can modulate, sense, or reprogram signal transduction in a controlled and context-dependent manner. We work at the interface of machine learning, structural biology, synthetic biology and biomedicine, combining deep learning-based structure prediction and generative design with experimental validation in cell-based systems.

Our research builds on and aims to further develop recent breakthroughs in diffusion models, sequence design networks, and third-generation structure prediction tools to design therapeutic binding domains, scaffolds, and synthetic receptors with precise spatial and functional control. Applications span from fundamental studies of receptor clustering and signaling to programmable receptors for cell therapy and regenerative medicine.

* Omics data cleaning, preprocessing, and quality checks
* Differential abundance analysis and statistical modeling
* Robust regression and sensitivity analysis for noisy biological datasets

Name: PanTum Detect
Description:
Der PanTum Detect ist ein Krebsscreening-Bluttest zur Früherkennung von Tumoren. 

Er kann mittels einer einfachen Blutentnahme bereits in frühen, symptomfreien Phasen Hinweise auf fast alle Tumorarten liefern - auch für solche, für die es heute noch keine etablierten gesetzlichen Früherkennungsangebote gibt. 

Der PanTum Detect basiert auf der EDIM-Technologie und detektiert die Enzyme TKTL1 und DNaseX (Apo10), die bei vielen Tumoren vermehrt gebildet werden. 

Der PanTum Detect stellt keine Krebsdiagnose, sondern gibt Hinweise auf eine mögliche Krebserkrankung, die in Folgeuntersuchungen (z.B. durch bildgebende Verfahren wie MRT oder PET/CT und histopathologische Verfahren) lokalisiert und bestätigt werden können. 

Der PanTum Detect weist eine Sensitivität von 95,2% und eine Spezifität von 99,5% auf.

Name: MATURE-NK
Description:
The MATURE-NK project is a Marie Sklodowska-Curie Innovative Training Network funded by the Horizon 2020 Framework Program of the EU. The network started in June 2018, will run over 4 years and aims to develop anti-cancer immunotherapies based on natural killer (NK) cells.

The consortium is formed by 13 groups located in 9 countries. It provides a balanced combination of basic and clinical research groups with industrial biotech partners. All principal investigators are recognized scientists in their field and 13 Early Stage Researchers (ESR or PhD students) have been recruited following a competitive assessment procedure.

The main objectives of MATURE-NK are to generate knowledge and to develop technologies for exploiting anti-tumor reactivity of NK cells. Reagents and cellular products based on NK cells will be tested in experimental cancer therapies providing the basis for promising future clinical application. As part of the Marie Sklodowska-Curie program, the project will focus on the promotion of excellence of European research and development and we will highlight the achievements of our fellows with a view to support their further career.

Name: Zendia GmbH
Description:
At Zendia we are committed to developing ultra sensitive POC (Point-Of-Care) diagnostic technologies in order to readily and easily detect infectious diseases at an early stage.  By efficiently detecting infections earlier, targeted treatment can be offered to patients sooner - not only decreasing the burden on healthcare systems, but ultimately leading to many lives saved.  At Zendia, we offer innovative solutions for global health problems.  

One major global health problem is malaria, which is a life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites.  Malaria is one of the most severe public health problems worldwide, and is a leading cause of disease and death in many developing countries. Nevertheless, the severity of malaria can be reduced and death can be prevented when diagnosed and treated in time.  At Zendia, we specialize in malaria diagnosis with a focus on detecting Plasmodium falciparum parasites. Current diagnostic tests for malaria fail to offer a universal approach.  At Zendia, our mission is to change that with our innovative diagnostic platform InfectoTest. With only 10 minutes of time, a drop of blood and an enrichment strategy, Infectotest provides quantitative single cell detection, revealing quick and easy patient infection status in real-time.

At Zendia, we detect to protect!

Description:
TRYPTO Therapeutics develops a novel class of Tryptophan Hydroxylase inhibitors for serotonin-dependent diseases.

We have developed and patented a novel class of TPH inhibitors (TPHi) with nanomolar potency in vitro to reduce the pathologically high serotonin synthesis in the periphery. The research products and services offered by Heidelberg Biolabs are based on thoroughly optimized protocols and various know-how developed at the German Cancer Research Center and University Hospital Heidelberg over the last decade. Our methodology secures the analysis of ultra-low RNA inputs with unprecedented efficacy, sensitivity, and robustness.

Our translational research initiative is being realized in the form of an innovative "Mi-Test" for preventive diagnostics of multiple pathological conditions based on extracellular RNA signatures in human blood and other biological fluids. The current version of Heidelberg Biolabs "Mi-Test" implies qPCR-based measurement of several miRNAs expressed exclusively in the myocardial cells, and which presence in the blood plasma can be a smart indicator of the ongoing cell death in the myocardium. Such surveillance of the health status by measuring organ-specific miRNAs (along with other circulating RNA species) in biofluids can be performed at point-of-care stations complementing the conventional blood tests in the future.

Name: CogniLens
Description:
CogniLens — Predictive Regulatory and Market Access Intelligence for Drugs and Medical Devices

Regulatory and design missteps cost the life sciences industry billions — delaying approvals and patient access.

CogniLens helps biotechs, medtechs, CROs, and regulatory consultants see risks months before submission.

What it does:
CogniLens analyzes draft clinical, technical, and regulatory documents to identify potential regulatory, scientific, and design risks up to 10× faster than manual review — reducing redesigns, protocol amendments, and submission queries by 30–50%.

How it works:
Built on a proprietary regulatory knowledge graph and an explainable AI scoring engine, CogniLens transforms complex regulatory guidelines into actionable insights and decision trees.
It provides clear explanations, linked guideline references, and targeted mitigation guidance — empowering faster, more compliant development.

Proven performance:
Trained on historical regulatory outcomes and documentation across drugs, devices, and combination products, CogniLens achieved precision 0.88 and recall 0.91 — demonstrating strong predictive alignment with real-world review results.

Platform modules:
• Protocol Lens – Predictive risk scoring for clinical trial protocols
• Design Lens – Detect gaps in device design documentation
• Submission Lens – Validate consistency across CTD modules and device dossiers
• Labeling Lens – Align claims and justifications with regulatory precedents

Data privacy & security by design:
CogniLens can be deployed in your secure environment, with EU/US-compliant hosting options available.

Learn more: www.cognilens.ai

Name: Scentum
Description:
Scentum utilizes quantum-based olfaction for molecule detection in both natural and industrial contexts. Our technology, inspired by the sensitive olfactory organs of living beings, enables the detection and interpretation of odor molecules even in minimal concentrations.

In doing so, we provide a groundbreaking alternative to conventional technologies such as electronic noses, which rely on high molecule concentrations and lack the necessary specificity to perform reliable measurements.

Our technology has a wide range of applications, including early disease diagnosis, the identification of hazardous substances, and the discovery of active compounds. With Scentum, we harness the power of quantum technology and biology to perceive the scents invisible to the human nose.

Key areas of interest include the mechanistic elucidation of receptor-mediated signal transduction and transcription-mediated regulatory processes in tumor cells. The Chair of Biochemistry and Molecular Medicine is part of the Institute of Biochemistry of the Faculty of Medicine at FAU.
Since 1978, the Institute of Biochemistry (until 1985 the Institute of Physiological Chemistry) in Fahrstraße has been home to two chairs and numerous research groups.

Name: ProP
Description:
ProP is an early-stage biotechnology in preparation. 

We are developing a next-generation therapeutic approach that combines rational protein design with mRNA-based delivery. 

Our current work focuses on a novel treatment strategy targeting both glucose control and metabolic liver disease, addressing a major unmet medical need at the intersection of type 2 diabetes and NAFLD. We design therapeutic concepts that enable tissue-specific activity by leveraging the body's endogenous machinery. By translating these designs into LNP-formulated mRNA, we aim to achieve efficient in vivo expression within a scalable and flexible platform. 

Building on a strong scientific foundation, secured intellectual property, and initial industry interest, we are now advancing towards defining the optimal delivery strategy and demonstrating proof-of-principle. 

We believe that the integration of protein design and mRNA delivery will open new avenues for programmable therapeutics.

Name: DNA ME
Description:
DNA ME makes DNA sequencing more accessible – for research laboratories, diagnostics providers and biotech companies.

From our development wet-lab in TecHHub, Germany to the world: We combine (ONT) nanopore hardware with our proprietary software pipeline – without the expensive GPU infrastructure required by traditional sequencing workflows.

Name: NanoAntenna Diagnostics (NADx)
Description:
Nanoantenna Diagnostics is an emerging LMU Munich spin-off developing ultra-sensitive nucleic acid detection technologies without molecular amplification. Our platform is based on DNA-engineered nanoantennas that enhance optical signals at the nanoscale, enabling direct detection of target sequences with high analytical sensitivity while reducing assay complexity.

By eliminating enzymatic amplification steps, we aim to provide robust and streamlined molecular analysis suitable for decentralized and resource-limited settings. The technology is adaptable to applications in food safety and risk management, supply chain traceability, and environmental monitoring, where rapid and reliable nucleic acid detection is required.

We were selected for Cohort 7 of the LMU Incubator program, where we further explored the translational potential of our technology. As we advance toward company formation, we are seeking partners, researchers, and public funding opportunities to develop and validate next-generation molecular sensing solutions.

Name: HeatDDR

Visit our website : https://www.heatddr.eu/

Name: Keynostic
Description:
Keynostic is developing a novel rapid testing platform for the personalized diagnosis and monitoring of individual biomarker deficiencies. Vitamin deficiency is our first use case, as it affects over 1 billion people worldwide, yet remains largely undetected due to the complexity and cost of current laboratory diagnostics. 

 The Problem:
Regular monitoring of biomarkers is essential. Especially for at-risk groups such as pregnant women, the elderly, people with chronic conditions, and individuals with specific dietary habits. Today, testing requires doctor visits and expensive laboratory equipment, making preventive and continuous monitoring inaccessible to most people.

 Our Solution:
Keynostic combines a rapid lateral-flow test strip with an ML-powered smartphone readout to deliver quantitative, personalized results directly at the point of care. —> fast, cost-effective, and easy to use at home. 

 Our Technology:
Our technology is based on research conducted at the Chair of Organic Chemistry II at the Technical University of Munich and was developed as part of a previous ERC Consolidator Grant and an ERC Proof-of-Concept Grant. The underlying platform enables a fundamentally new approach to biomarker detection. 

 Where We Stand:
Since April 2026, Keynostic has been funded by EXIST Research Transfer, one of Germany’s most competitive deep-tech funding programs from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWK). This marks the official transition of our technology from research at TU Munich to building a scalable commercial product. 

 Our Network:
We collaborate with diagnostic labs, physicians, and nutrition experts to validate our solution against clinical reality. 

 Munich, Germany
 
 Join us on our journey to make personalized biomarker monitoring accessible to everyone.

We use engineered enzymes and reaction engineering to make complex terpenes faster, more predictable and more resource-efficiently accessible. Our platform enables improved routes to known natural products and opens access to new-to-nature terpenes with differentiated properties.

Cyterra combines deep enzymology, biocatalysis, organic chemistry, terpene handling, mechanism-guided engineering and disciplined scale-up thinking. We turn ideas to gram-scale samples in months.

Name: Functional Neuroconnectomics Lab
Description:
The team is led by our Principal Investigator, Dr Martin K. Schwarz. The lab is part of Institute for Experimental Epileptology and Cognition Research, and its affliated with University of Bonn. Our dedication to pushing the boundaries of neuroscience continues to drive us forward. 
Our group focuses on the functional characterization of neural circuits that orchestrate state-dependent behaviors, with a special emphasis on social interactions. We are pioneering automated behavioral detection (now-casting) of disease-indicative phenotypes, utilizing state-of-the-art technologies to monitor various modalities of behavior, including vocalization and gait analysis. 
To achieve our research goals, we employ advanced techniques such as ultrasonic recordings, functional ultrasound imaging, light sheet fluorescence microscopy, and fiber photometry imaging. These tools allow us to study ethologically relevant information in freely moving mice, providing deeper insights into their behavior and neural mechanisms.

The Problem: Women's health is facing a trillion-dollar innovation gap. For too long, research has excluded women, funding has been scarce, and progress has been unacceptably slow. The result is a healthcare system that leaves half the population with more questions than answers.

Our Vision: We envision a future where biology doesn't limit potential. A future where menopause is optional and where reproductive health receives the funding and attention it deserves.

Description: Immunhistochemistry (IHC) on formalin fixed tissues is a major application for antibodies. However, most of the commercially available antibodies do not perform appropriately in IHC. The few antibodies that do work well are usually not known to the scientific community because the existing antibodies are not adequately validated. Cross-reactivities (strong binding to another than the target protein) and non-specific binding are the major causes for false IHC results. Many established and IVD/IVDR classified antibodies suffer from significant cross-reactivities resulting in false positivity’s. Appropriate validation of antibodies inevitably  requires the use of large numbers of different tissues. Tissue microarrays (TMAs) enable the simultaneous analysis of more than 600 tissues per section. Studies including thousands of tissues can be executed within days if appropriate TMAs are available. Such clinical studies can evaluate and demonstrate the clinical utility of antibodies and combination of antibodies very rapidly.

Name: ASH Therapeutics
Description:
Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is a treatment mainly used for blood-related cancers and some other severe diseases. During this process, stem cells from healthy donors are transferred into patient's bodies to replace damaged or diseased cells. While this treatment can be life-saving, it comes with serious risks and complications like GVHD.

GVHD is a complex medical condition that often occurs after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Thereby, the donated stem cells perceive the recipient's body as foreign and initiate an immune response against it, which leads to severe complications and prevents a broader application of these transplantations. 

We have developed a targeted therapy designed to effectively modulate immune responses. This breakthrough not only has the potential to significantly reduce the risk of complications like GVHD, but also offers promise in treating a wide range of autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. By fine-tuning the immune system's behavior, our solution aims to maximize the benefits of transplantation and other therapies, thereby improving patient outcomes and expanding the scope of treatable diseases.

Name: CVENT H2020
Description:
CVENT: European Union’s Horizon 2020 programme
Risk assessment of plaque rupture and future cardiovascular events by multi-spectral photoacoustic imaging

Vulnerable atherosclerotic carotid plaques, an age and lifestyle related vascular disease, remain a major cause of death for men and women at middle age and is also a hallmark of generalized cardiovascular diseases (CVD) involving other critical vascular regions like the coronary arteries. Every patient exhibiting symptoms of partial occlusion of the carotid arteries is examined with ultrasound (US) because a matured carotid plaque is potentially vulnerable to rupture. When that happens, the content of the lesion entering the blood stream can cause stroke. In the EU this affects over 1 million people annually. According to the guidelines, the patient is operated on, if a 70-99% occlusion of the artery is found. However, only one out of nine operations is effective (Barnett 1998; Rothwell 2003). Even worse, 19 operations need to be done to prevent a single stroke. Hence, the current method to assess plaque vulnerability is insufficient.

The existence of intra-plaque haemorrhages is the main indicator of rupture-prone atherosclerotic plaques in general. The revolutionary step forward in functional photoacoustic imaging (PA) to be made by the CVENT consortium is providing in-vivo functional imaging of vulnerable plaques in the carotid artery for screening, in-depth diagnosis and monitoring.

CVENT is focused on CVD patients to screen, diagnose and monitor carotid plaque vulnerability, by stratifying patients into higher and lower risk groups, this leads to a reduction in overtreatment, better allocation of healthcare cost, and thus contribute to the sustainability of the health care system in Europe.

Name: LAPTI (SECRETUM)
Description:
We are building LAPTI - a Digital SELEX engine for aptamer discovery.

Aptamer development is a major bottleneck in biosensor and diagnostic innovation: traditional SELEX is slow, expensive (€20k-€100k per target), and limits iteration. This creates high entry barriers and slows down breakthroughs.

Our solution replaces months of wet-lab selection with in-silico simulations.
We combine AI-driven sequence generation with a physics-based validation engine for folding and binding - enabling fast exploration of sequence space without sacrificing correctness.

 How it works:
• 3D model of the target molecule
• AI proposes aptamer candidates
• Physics engine validates binding & folding
• Best candidates are iteratively optimized
→ Synthesis-ready structures with predicted affinity

 Validation:
An anti-creatinine aptamer, designed entirely in our engine, was successfully used in the SensUs 2024 competition, demonstrating high affinity and real experimental performance.

We are continuing to develop the platform and actively preparing for new pitches and public appearances.
